standard_prerequisites.use: Control respectively the matching structure around A and the number of bipartitions of the relevant set, which together give the probabilistic contradiction.

core_obligations: Assume the contrary: fix p in the window and suppose the deficiency of G_p is at least two while the set A of its Gallai-Edmonds decomposition has size greater than the threshold (proof line 1421).
Organise the D part: split the components of G_p[D] into singletons and non-singletons and record the parameters a, r and h (proof lines 1422-1426).

Convert the structural relations into an edge count: use the exact edge-counting identity for the Gallai-Edmonds parameters and the strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph to relate the size of A to the boundary of D (proof lines 1426-1600, the author's main body of estimates).

Count the colourings and contradict the assumption: apply the weighted counting bound for bipartitions of a set with a small boundary to show that the probability of the configuration is o(1), which contradicts the assumption and proves the bound (proof lines 1600-1635).
proof_roadmap: 反设：固定 p，假设亏数 r >= 2 而 Gallai-Edmonds 分解中的 A 大于阈值 u_0。
先用 Gallai-Edmonds 参数的精确边计数恒等式与辅助二部图的严格 Hall 不等式，把 |A| 与 D 的边界联系起来。
再用边界小的集合的加权二划分计数上界，把该构型出现的概率压到 o(1)，得到矛盾。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the size bound for the set A of the Gallai-Edmonds decomposition in the non-bipartite case (author lemma at source lines 1416-1419, label lem:nonbipartite-ge). Its proof (source lines 1420-1635) is the longest in the paper and is a probabilistic argument built on the decomposition: it fixes p in the window, assumes the deficiency is at least two and A larger than the threshold, and then combines the exact edge-counting identity for the Gallai-Edmonds parameters, the strict Hall inequality for the auxiliary bipartite graph and the weighted counting bound for bipartitions of a set with a small boundary to force a contradiction. The chain is what makes the random part of the main theorem work in the non-bipartite case, and the author notes that the bipartite case needs separate treatment. H2.
